FN-SL2NH58-1
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 330
Committee: County and Municipal Government Sponsor: Senator Dan Roberts
Analyst: Mathieu Fuller Date: 04/22/2025
Senate Bill 330 as introduced would increase the obligations of any municipal water works
board either serving water customers or that has assets in four or more counties other than the
county where the authorizing municipality is principally located that is converted into a regional
water board pursuant to the provisions of this bill, for board member compensation by: (1) a
minimum of $120,000 annually (adjusted for CPI increases annually) for the five board
members appointed pursuant to the provisions of this bill; (2) an undetermined amount for the
reimbursement of necessary expenditures incurred in carrying out board member duties; and (3)
an undetermined amount to report certain financial information to the local legislative
delegation representing the counties served by the regional water boards and the Alabama
Department of Examiners of Public Accounts, and to post on the board's website for public
access.
This bill would also increase the obligations of the Attorney General to: (1) ensure appointees to
the board are properly qualified; and (2) prevent or recoup amounts paid by a regional water
board to municipalities or counties in violation of the provisions of this bill.

FN-SL2NH58-2
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 330
Committee: Commerce and Small Business Sponsor: Senator Dan Roberts
Analyst: Mathieu Fuller Date: 04/28/2025
Senate Bill 330 as passed the Senate would increase the obligations of certain municipal water
works boards, which would be converted to a regional water board pursuant to the provisions of
this bill, by: (1) a maximum of $60,000 annually due to the change in membership and
compensation of the board of directors pursuant to the provisions of this bill; and (2) an
undetermined amount dependent on any increases in compensation of the board due to
adjustments tied to the Consumer Price Index, as provided by this bill.
This bill would also increase the administrative obligations of these boards to report certain
financial information to the respective local legislative delegation and the Alabama Department
of Examiners of Public Accounts and to post this information on the board's website.
This bill would also increase the administrative obligations of the Attorney General to: (1)
ensure appointees to the board are properly qualified; and (2) prevent or recoup amounts paid by
a regional water board to municipalities or counties in violation of the provisions of this bill.
